No warning came; the board maintained expectations, as the MAR-silence argument predicted.
This positioning claim cannot be checked against the release.
The interim was 36.0p (+10%), covered 1.1x by adjusted EPS, exactly as predicted.

surprise_size_note: The release was in line and fully pre-guided. The -1.9% move is small and proportionate; a CFO departure was the only unscheduled item.

findings_scored.note: The release did not confirm any Meta-settlement money ('too early to form a definitive view') and the run-up partly unwound. Correct sign.
H1 revenue -3.9%, no FY upgrade, FX caveat added and a broker cut FY26 revenue by £1.5m. Correct sign.

surprise_size_note: A moderate move for a release with essentially no new numbers; it reads as the pre-print, news-free run-up deflating rather than as a surprise.

EPS EUR4.80 vs consensus EUR5.57 (-13.8%, per goldesel.de: https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/kws-saat-steigert-nettoergebnis-um-13-verfehlt-erwartungen-aktie-verliert-85).

prior_update.note: No pre-release. The last numbers were the 9M release of 2026-05-12.

moved_on_evidence: Boersennews: shares down ~11% intraday, closed -6.9%. It cites lower beet/corn acreage and FY26/27 margin guidance at the low end of the corridor that 'lags consensus'. Sales and EPS also missed.

findings_scored.note: No pre-release, and the results day was sold again (7th in a row).
Guidance came in soft: margin 19-20% against the 19-21% band. EUR29m licensing one-off confirmed.
SZVG delivery-rights point not in the release. KWS instead cited smaller sugarbeet acreage as a drag, so the direction was wrong.
EBITDA EUR343.1m, not ~EUR375m. Adjusted margin 19.3% is the lower part of the band, not the upper half, and sales missed flat.

surprise_size_note: -9% fits a triple miss (sales, adjusted margin, EPS -14% vs consensus) plus soft guidance. The size matched the surprise; the hunter's reported-quarter call was wrong.

release_headline: Quadient H1 2026 results: Digital ARR up 13% on an annualized organic basis. Strong free cash flow of €34 million (plus separate release: 'Quadient announces intention to sell Lockers business. As a first step, sale of UK open network signed for €65 million.')
print_vs_bar_note: The bar is a range (-2%..+2% organic), not a point. H1 organic revenue -2.0% (Q2 -2.4%) sits at the bottom edge; current EBIT €57m, -5.9% organic; Mail EBITDA margin 24.9% (-0.6pt). No sourced H1 consensus.
guidance_detail: FY26 guidance restated ex-Lockers under IFRS 5 (organic -3%..+1%, Digital EBITDA margin >19%, Mail >24%) and called 'confirmed'; leverage target improved to 1.2x from ~1.5x on the UK lockers sale proceeds.

prior_update.note: Only a Q2 Digital bookings KPI was pre-disclosed (>20%); the half's revenue and profit were not.

moved_on_evidence: Low confidence: no article explains the 24 Sep fall. The day's news was the Lockers review outcome (UK open network sold for €65m, rest to be sold, €11m net loss from discontinued operations) alongside a soft core half (EBIT -5.9% organic, net income €9m vs €20m). The stock had already risen ~3.9% on 23 Sep before the release (Yahoo close €12.92), so part of the fall was the day giving that back.

findings_scored.note: The Lockers review update did come on this release: UK open network sold for €65m and the rest put up for sale. The market read it as no better than the price already held; the +2.5 sign was wrong.
Q2 Digital bookings >20% and French e-invoicing bookings up eleven-fold confirmed; FY guidance not cut. The 'no cut' call was right, but it did not lift the stock.
The AMF threshold filing is not in the release and was not checked here.
Lockers weakness confirmed indirectly: the unit was classified as discontinued with an impairment-driven €11m net loss.

surprise_size_note: Small move for a release that resolved a strategic review; the outcome looked roughly as expected, and part of the -2.2% was giving back the +3.9% pre-release gain on 23 Sep.
source: post-mortem filled 2026-09-28 by a general-purpose subagent from the release and same-day coverage; secondary sources flagged in notes

Signal right in direction: the board did soften FY revenue expectations; the option-hurdle fact itself was not in the release.
Buyback of up to GBP 2.5m confirmed (commenced 27 Jul, completing by end-Sep); stock fell from the top of that supported rally.

Holder/free-float facts not tested by the release; double-digit reaction consistent with thin float.
